steps.label: The two species
lines: OFFICINARUM were crossed to get a better yield.
steps.why: Two species of the same genus can be crossed, which is what let breeders combine their separate advantages.
common_mistakes: Naming a different genus. Both are SACCHARUM species.
Naming one species. The question asks which TWO.
steps.memory_tip: Both are Saccharum: barberi and officinarum.

steps.label: What each contributed
steps.margin_note: What each parent had and what the cross achieved.

steps.why: Each parent supplied what the other lacked, which is the whole logic of a deliberate interspecific cross.
common_mistakes: Saying both had high sugar. Only OFFICINARUM did.
Giving the names with no reason for the cross. The reason is the second mark.
steps.memory_tip: One brought the climate, the other brought the sugar.
